business_scope.primary_industry_name: Self-Insurance Risk Underwriting for Multinational Enterprise Groups

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: BITs with United States (1995), China (2005), Mexico (1997), Argentina (1997), Brazil (1994), Chile (1991) and multiple other Latin American nations; extensive DTAs and FTAs

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent national authority of UBO country of residence

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory PEP, OFAC, UN, EU, and Spanish domestic sanctions screening for all UBOs, shareholders, and directors prior to incorporation filing

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Spanish language using Latin script; no transliteration required
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Generic terms such as Banco, Caja, Seguros, Reaseguros without prior approval
Protected company names or those confusing with public entities
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Administrative appeal to the notary or competent registry authority within 10 business days if name is rejected

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual offices are permissible for SL companies provided the registered office meets legal requirements and commercial substance is demonstrated
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low (5-10% for random checks); higher if AML red flags identified

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Corporate legal consultation and due diligence
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff for SL plus prevailing market rate
Fixed statutory fee for SL incorporation

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO beneficial ownership verification and screening

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT); electronic portal: Sede Electrónica de la AEAT (https://sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For an ES_SL incorporated in Spain, the NIF (Número de Identificación Fiscal) is applied for during incorporation through the public deed before the Mercantile Registry (Registro Mercantil) and AEAT, using provisional NIF certificate plus Form 036 census registration. A non-resident entity without permanent establishment must appoint a Spanish resident tax representative and file Form 036 with AEAT, attaching certified incorporation documents, statutory articles, and power of attorney. The NIF for a non-resident legal entity is a 'W' prefix followed by digits and a control character.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election exists in Spanish domestic law. Tax entity classification is fixed by statute. Eligible groups may elect the consolidated tax group regime (Régimen de Consolidación Fiscal) under Corporate Income Tax Law (LIS) Articles 58-70; holding companies may elect the ETVE participation exemption regime (Régimen de Entidades de Tenencia de Valores Extranjeras). Anti-hybrid mismatch rules derived from EU ATAD apply, overriding treaty and domestic characterisation mismatches.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (IVA - Impuesto sobre el Valor Añadido)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general turnover threshold for Spanish resident entities; VAT registration is mandatory before commencement of any taxable business activity. For intra-community distance sales to Spain by non-resident EU suppliers, an annual EUR 10,000 threshold applies.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: The SII (Suministro Inmediato de Información) requires almost-real-time invoice reporting to AEAT by taxpayers with annual turnover above EUR 6,000,000 and by VAT groups; invoice data must be transmitted within 4 business days. Electronic invoicing between Spanish businesses and in cross-border B2B transactions must comply with Ley Crea y Crece (Regulation RD 1007/2023), but no fiscal stamping or government pre-clearance is required.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods to destinations outside the EU are zero-rated (exempt with input VAT crediting) under Article 21 LIVA. Services supplied to non-EU recipients are generally zero-rated when the place of supply is outside the EU under the B2B rules. Reinsurance services are mandatorily VAT-exempt under Article 20.Uno.16 LIVA and are not eligible for zero-rating or option to tax; input VAT on costs related to a captive reinsurance SPV is generally non-recoverable.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DUA - Documento Único Administrativo) duly accepted by AEAT
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill proving physical departure from the EU customs territory
Inward Remittance Certificate or SWIFT/bank statement evidencing receipt of export payment
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: AEAT may retrospectively claw back zero-rated output VAT plus default interest where export documentary evidence is missing or false. Penalties for fraudulent or unjustified zero-rating range from 50% to 150% of the tax benefit under Article 184 LGT; loss of input VAT deduction rights may also be imposed, and criminal tax fraud liability under Article 305 Penal Code applies where the loss exceeds EUR 120,000.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Spain, as a founding member of the Eurozone and the European Union, maintains a regime of full capital and current account convertibility. There are no restrictions on the repatriation of profits, dividends, or capital contributions for Spanish SL entities. However, all FX transactions are subject to mandatory reporting to the Banco de España through the Integrated Administrative System (SIAE) for statistical purposes, and compliance with AML/CFT directives is mandatory. Profit remittance hurdles are minimal, limited primarily to tax withholding at source where applicable under Spanish or double tax treaty rules.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Spain does not impose any mandatory surrender or conversion requirements on export proceeds. Exporters are required to file export declarations with the Spanish Customs Agency (AEAT) within specified timelines, but funds may be freely converted into euros or other currencies and repatriated. Companies must ensure proper invoicing and documentation to support tax deductions and avoid penalties under the General Taxation Law.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Digital EMI providers such as N26 Business or Revolut Business are viable for corporate treasury functions but operate under strict oversight by the Banco de España and the European Banking Authority. Offshore digital EMIs are feasible with proper licensing and structuring, subject to compliance with MiCA regulations for electronic money institutions. Legal constraints include enhanced KYC/AML protocols, potential restrictions on cross-border transfers, and the need for local entity registration to avoid regulatory sanctions.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Initial KYC and onboarding for Spanish SL entities typically requires physical presence of directors or authorized representatives for in-person interviews and document verification at tier-1 banks. Remote onboarding is permitted for subsequent account management using advanced digital identification methods such as Cl@ve PIN or electronic signatures, provided the entity is already established in Spain.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Complex beneficial ownership structures or unexplained source of wealth
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Beneficial ownership declaration in accordance with Law 10/2010 on the prevention of money laundering, corporate structure diagram, and independent audit reports confirming the legitimacy of funds

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk sector classification as captive reinsurance
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Valid reinsurance authorization from the Spanish Directorate General of Insurance and Pension Funds (DGSFP), reinsurance contracts, and third-party actuarial or risk management certifications

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inconsistent financial statements or lack of commercial substance
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed business plan, proof of economic activity in Spain, and supporting documentation from group entities demonstrating the captive nature of the reinsurance operations

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections are processed through SWIFT MT103 or MT202 messages using purpose codes such as 'CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION' or 'EQUITY INJECTION'. Verification protocols require board resolutions, shareholder agreements, and source of funds evidence. All wires must be accompanied by tax identification numbers and purpose codes compliant with Spanish tax authorities for VAT and withholding tax purposes.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound disbursements for reinsurance settlements are cleared via SWIFT MT103 with purpose codes like 'REINSURANCE PREMIUM' or 'LOSS PAYMENT'. Commercial Letters of Credit are permissible but less common for pure reinsurance. All outflows must comply with transfer pricing documentation requirements under Spanish law and be supported by underlying trade or reinsurance agreements.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Forward FX contracts for hedging currency exposures
Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) for emerging market currencies
Currency swaps for multi-currency liquidity optimization and risk management

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts approval and deposit (Depósito de Cuentas Anuales)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Provincial Mercantile Registry of the registered office; publication in BORME by Registro Mercantil Central
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Approval by shareholders within 6 months after fiscal year-end; deposit with the Registry within 1 month after approval. For a 31 December year-end: latest deposit by 31 July.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Registry closure (cierre registral): no document of the company can be registered while the deposit is outstanding; administrative fines up to EUR 60,000 per overdue year; persistent non-compliance after at least 3 consecutive years enables the Registrar to initiate cancellation of the company's registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return and settlement (Modelo 200)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 25 calendar days after the 6-month post-year-end period (for a calendar-year taxpayer: 1–25 July of the following year).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing surcharge: 5% of tax due if filed within 3 months, 10% within 6 months, 15% within 12 months, 20% after 12 months, plus late-payment interest; penalties up to 50% of tax assessment for false or incomplete filing.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Mercantile Registry beneficial-ownership register and, for supervised re/insurance entities, the DGSFP
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Confirmation is submitted with the annual accounts deposit for the reporting year; any ownership change must be declared within one month of the event and in all cases before the next general meeting.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: AML administrative fines under Law 10/2010 for failures in UBO reporting; loss of reliable registry certification; for captives, supervisory penalties up to EUR 150,000 and possible withdrawal of reinsurance authorization.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Related-party transactions information return (Modelo 232) – intragroup reinsurance operations
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 1–25 July of the year following the reporting period, or the equivalent 25-calendar-day window after the 6-month post-year-end date for non-calendar fiscal years.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or materially incomplete filing triggers penalties under Article 198 of the General Tax Law, from EUR 200 per data item up to EUR 10,000 per return; inaccuracies may also be assessed under transfer-pricing review.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Solvency and Financial Condition Report (SFCR) and regular supervisory report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Seguros y Fondos de Pensiones (DGSFP)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 14 weeks after the fiscal year-end (for a 31 December year-end: by early April of the following year); ORSA summary is maintained internally and filed in accordance with DGSFP protocols.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Serious infraction regime under Royal Legislative Decree 20/2015: administrative fines, suspension of new business, and possible revocation of the captive reinsurance license; DGSFP may impose remedial measures.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit in all cases for licensed captive reinsurance undertakings. For other Spanish SLs, audit is compulsory when, at two consecutive fiscal year-ends, the company meets at least two of three thresholds: balance-sheet total above EUR 2,850,000; net turnover above EUR 5,700,000; average headcount above 50.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Individual statutory accounts under Spanish Local GAAP (Plan General de Contabilidad, PGC), with the insurance-specific adaptation for re/insurance companies; consolidated accounts under EU-IFRS; Solvency II valuation principles for regulatory capital and financial condition reports.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Spain does not require an independent annual UBO declaration separate from the annual accounts deposit. The SL must keep its UBO register permanently updated, declare any transfer of qualifying shareholdings (10%, 25%, 50% and controlling ownership) within one month, and, through the annual audit and accounts deposit, confirm the accuracy of registered ownership. For captive reinsurers, the DGSFP annual reporting protocol includes confirmation of the ultimate parent, direct reinsurance counterparties and group ownership chain.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Libro Registro de Socios)
Register of Directors (Libro Registro de Administradores)
Annual Accounts and Inventory Book (Libro de Inventarios y Cuentas Anuales)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 10,000–28,000 per annum for a captive reinsurance SL audit and review of statutory registers

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% (Ley 27/2014, Art. 29.1 LIS). Reduced 15% rate for newly created SOCIMIs? No, for new entities: 15% for first two tax periods with positive taxable base (Art. 29.1 LIS), subject to substantive activity and non-asset-holding conditions.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: New-entity reduced rate 15% for two years (Art. 29.1 LIS); R&D&I tax credits (25% R&D, 8% technological innovation); employment credits (0%-50%); 95% participation exemption on qualifying dividends/CG (Art. 21 LIS); NOL offset with limits 70%/50%/25% (Art. 26 LIS); DTA and EU directives.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited (indefinite carryforward; Art. 26.1 LIS); offset cap 70% of positive tax base for turnover ≥ €1M (50% for ≥ €20M; 25% for ≥ €60M); minimum €1M always offsettable.
